concrete_scene.heading: Worked public-safe simulation gate: the button survives, judgment does not
concrete_scene.actor_or_system: A non-operational command simulation, one accountable decision maker, five available time units, and three off-ramps
concrete_scene.attempted_action: Admit a public-safe simulation only after mission, legal, role, effect, observation, meaningful-judgment, interaction, safe-posture, off-ramp, expiry, remedy, and residual fields are bound.
concrete_scene.observable_outcome: The authored 5-versus-3 time margin and 3-versus-2 off-ramp margin permit only simulation eligibility; shrinking time or off-ramps rejects even while the human interface and approval button remain present.
concrete_scene.failed_or_tested_boundary: The scene tests whether interface presence or component evidence can substitute for practical judgment and strategic interaction review; two collision pairs show they cannot.
concrete_scene.residual_owner: Accountable command, legal review, affected-population, incident, remedy, decommissioning, and strategic-interaction owners retain every real-world obligation.
concrete_scene.evidence_boundary: The dossier is deliberately public-safe and non-operational; it authorizes no weapon, target, deployment, use of force, lawful-use claim, escalation claim, strategic-stability claim, or publication of operational detail.

worked_trace.heading: Worked public-safe simulation gate: the button survives, judgment does not
worked_trace.maximum_inference: The finite review demonstrates meaningful-judgment and interaction fields, adverse monotonic rejection, and two non-identifiability boundaries; it establishes no weapon authorization, lawful use, real control, escalation reduction, safety, or strategic stability.

counterexample_or_simpler_baseline: The simpler baseline counts a human confirmation interface as control. The chapter requires sufficient time, information, competence, independence, intervention reach, alternatives, and off-ramps across the command situation.
readable_claim: A person behind an approval button is not meaningful human control when the system withholds time, evidence, alternatives, or practical power to intervene. Component accuracy cannot repair that missing judgment.
normative_rule: Before any public-safe simulation proceeds, bind the mission, legal boundary, decision role, affected population, effect envelope, accountable authority, required decision time, observation trust, abstention, safe posture, adversary interaction, off-ramps, expiry, and remedy. Any missing or shrinking judgment condition blocks the scenario.

formal_binding.anchor: governed as a command-and-interaction system: deployment requires a declared mission and legal boundary

caveat_consolidation.local_caveat: The worked gate states once that it is a non-operational simulation dossier and cannot authorize a weapon or use of force.
caveat_consolidation.consolidated_disposition: Legal, observation, human judgment, effect, doctrine, adversary interaction, escalation, secrecy, remedy, decommissioning, and strategic-stability limits remain separately visible.

bookkeeping_surface_disposition: The time and off-ramp margins remain because their deterioration drives rejection; full 45-axis and theorem inventories remain in formal evidence surfaces.

editorial_diagnostics.mega_sentence_disposition: The new projections isolate meaningful judgment and admission logic from the complete command-and-interaction claim.
editorial_diagnostics.hedge_disposition: The public-safe non-operational boundary is stated once while distinct legal, strategic, human-control, observation, and remedy limits remain.
editorial_diagnostics.table_disposition: The decision-role and assurance tables remain because they distinguish system positions and evidence burdens, not project bookkeeping.

non_claims: The public-safe dossier contains no target, weapon, evasion, or operational-use guidance.
The finite review does not establish lawful use, meaningful control, safety, or strategic stability.
The editorial revision does not move chapter-core support or release state.
